alternatives.argument: The item is a complete local definition: it specifies the finite geometric mesh, integrable target, square-integrable approximations, marginal-preserving adjacent-level coupling, correction law, independent within-level copies, independent cross-level blocks, and estimator. It imports no result from the thesis. Giles §2 and the complete Reisinger lecture slides independently cover the hierarchy and telescoping construction.

The complete local proof derives level-mean unbiasedness and variance from the exact IID Monte Carlo mean-moment theorem, telescopes the coupling marginals, uses finite expectation linearity, and applies the exact MSE/covariance identity to independent level blocks. The exact remaining source dependencies are the local hierarchy definition, thm-iid-monte-carlo-mean-moments, cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound, and thm-error-ledger-mse-covariance-identity. Giles §2 and the complete Reisinger lecture independently present the estimator and variance calculation.

The complete local proof selects the bias cutoff level, constructs positive integer sample counts by ceiling the square-root variance/work allocation, proves the MSE split using the estimator lemma, bounds the integer-rounding work, and evaluates the geometric sum separately for beta>1, beta=1, and 0<beta<1. Its only mathematical inputs are the local hierarchy definition and local estimator-moment/MSE lemma. Giles Theorem 3.1 and the complete Reisinger lecture provide independent treatments; the theorem states the absolute-bias premise needed by the proof.

The example is fully checked locally: it normalizes the density, computes the exact target and weak bias by integrating the two shifted threshold probabilities, enumerates the two signed crossing intervals under the shared (X,S) coupling, derives the correction mean and variance, proves the variance is bounded above and below by positive multiples of sqrt(h), and applies the local complexity theorem. It depends only on the hierarchy definition and the abstract complexity theorem. Giles §3.1 independently motivates the discontinuous-payoff half-rate regime; the exact distributional construction and every bound are proved in the item.
